name: Lalana Chinantec
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Mugele, Robert L. 1982. Tone and ballistic syllable in Lalana Chinantec. PhD diss., University of Texas at Austin; also Rensch & Rensch 1966, The Lalana Chinantec syllable (SIL Mexico Workpapers). No open copy found.
earlier_scan.note: Chinantec prosody is ballistic/controlled syllable + tone; Mugele 1982 is the dedicated study.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, reference list for lala1270 (19 entries) and for the Chinantec family
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Confirms the only Lalana-specific phonological works are Rensch & Rensch 1966, Mugele 1982 (hhtype phonology), Mugele 1984; everything else is comparative (Rensch 1966/1968/1976/1977/1978/1989), literacy or texts. No grammar, no dictionary, no JIPA illustration exists for Lalana.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Lalana-Tepinapa Chinantec' (accessed 2026-09-17); SIL Mexico 'Chinantecan Family' page; SIL/SIL Mexico bibliography listings for cnl (Wayback 2015/2016)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology or stress; the SIL listings give the same set of Lalana works as Glottolog plus primers and Scripture.

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. 1989. An etymological dictionary of the Chinantec languages (Studies in Chinantec Languages 1; SIL & UTA Publications in Linguistics 87). Dallas: SIL. xii+173 pp.
sources.note: Comparative only. Proto-Chinantec prosodic elements are two tones *H, *L (combinations HL, LH, HLH) and a 'ballistic accent' that 'could occur with both tones and all three combinations' (p. 12); Lalana (Ll) is said to have lost length in accented syllables closed by *? (p. 13). No statement on word-stress placement in any daughter language. fetched sources from a Wayback snapshot of the SIL file (SIL file host returns 403 here).

sources.citation: Mugele, Robert L. 1976. Lalana Chinantec y-. Why? Work Papers of the Summer Institute of Linguistics, University of North Dakota Session 20, Article 3, pp. 1-38. DOI 10.31356/silwp.vol20.03
sources.note: Silent on stress. Morphophonemics of verb stems (vowel shifts, palatalization). Note 2 (p. 37) restates the Rensch & Rensch 1966 phoneme inventory: prosody phonemes = vowel length, vowel nasalization, tone (1 high, 2 mid, 3 low), plus post-vocalic h reanalysed as the prosodic feature 'ballistic syllable' (marked by acute accent); stress is not mentioned anywhere in the 38 pages (grep of scanned for stress/accent/prominence).
